correctness.rationale: The bounded-Lipschitz norm N_lambda(x)=max|x_i|+lambda(max x_i-min x_i) equals |(M+m)/2|+s(M-m)/2 for s=1+2lambda. The claimed sign-vector vertices and their polar determine {||y||_1<=s, |sum y|<=1}; extrema integration gives primal volume 2^n/s^(n-1). Orthant decomposition of a simplex difference body yields the exact diagonal-slab density q_n(t), and the signed-polynomial integration P_n(a)=Prob(|sum Y_i|<=a) gives the polar volume. Even, nonincreasing section densities with nonconstancy for n>=3 show strict monotonicity of s P_n(1/s); n=2 is constant. Stirling/Vandermonde and variance 2n/((n+1)(n+2)) prove two limits. Independently re-expanded and exactly normalized the density polynomial for n=2..9; checked independent rational verifier source. These tests are finite; analytical section arguments give all n,s.
residual_risks: Finite verification does not prove all quantified real/dimensional claims; the proof was independently reconstructed and checked against boundary cases.

value.rationale: The exact interpolation distinguishes sum-form bounded-Lipschitz norms from both cube and anchored extreme metric limits. A new closed slab polynomial, sharp strictness for each n>=3, and high-dimensional limits give a natural finite Banach-space invariant useful independently of a global Mahler conjecture.
